inspiration: repipe round 3 need arm-literal-pool-string; the sibling of kuna_picbase (the i386 PIC-base fold), and the shape of Ghidra's reference analyzer defining a pc-relative literal target as data before anything else reads it
hypothesis_status: no hypothesis was offered; the captain's T_TRIAGE reading (the reference scan does not follow an ARM literal-pool load) is upheld exactly

promoted_probe.why: the acceptance's own target is `binary_source: dataset` and CI has no dataset; the vendored fixture is a 735-byte hand-assembled A32 ELF carrying the same defect plus the three refusals

no_option_because: Track `tooling`. The change is confined to the on-demand cross-reference index (`listing::xrefs::build`), which is read only by `kuna xrefs`, `kuna strings` and `decompile-all`'s xref/reachability sections. No p-code, prototype or emitted C depends on it, and all four parity gates are byte-identical. `picbase`, the closest precedent, DID take an option -- it is a speculative abstract machine whose ownership claim needed an escape hatch; this is one dereference of immutable image content and has no comparable failure mode. The lease on phases.toml / the catalog counters was held by another builder this round in any case.

sweep.method: `kuna strings --json` over 15 images, before/after, with both binaries rebuilt and each independently re-checked against the witness probe before use (a sibling agent clobbered a first pair under generic /tmp names)

oracle.what: capstone A32 linear sweep (restarting past undecodable words) + the ELF symtab + kuna's own reported function extents -- no kuna code in the reference path
oracle.note: every outlier resolved to a pool load the oracle's own sweep missed, confirmed with `kuna xrefs --to`; none was a fabricated edge

speed.method: interleaved before/after, 7 repeats, min-of-N (the box carried other builders throughout, so medians swing +-20% on byte-identical output and are not used)
speed.note: the walk itself costs ~1%. The first measurement showed +53% on `kuna strings` for u-boot, and it was NOT the follow: `ConsoleProgram::find_entry_at` rebuilds and linearly scans the whole function inventory per call, which is free while no string has an owner and 0.85 s once 1,792 of them do. strings.rs now reads that inventory once; the output is byte-identical (checked on four images).

decisions.claim: The followed reference is attributed to the loading instruction, not to the pool word that holds the address.
decisions.evidence: `kuna strings` answers `functions` by mapping each reference's `from` address to the function containing it. A pool word is data and lies in no function, so an edge filed from 0x86e4 would answer the agent's question with another address instead of a name. Filing from 0x862c also means the new edge inherits EXACTLY the attribution the pre-existing `read` edge to the pool word already had -- same `st.file(vma, ...)` call site, same vma -- so no new ownership logic exists to be wrong.

decisions.claim: A LOAD's address varnode is pointer-sized whatever the access width is, so the pointer-size gate has to read the LOAD's output.
decisions.evidence: `ldrh r0,[0x1003c]` lifts to `u:2 = *(ram, r0x1003c)`: the address operand is a 4-byte ram varnode and the output is 2 bytes. Taking the width from the address varnode followed the pool word of a HALFWORD load -- caught on the vendored fixture, whose `narrow_read` was attributed to a string before the fix and is not after. Pinned by `a_narrow_load_of_a_pool_word_files_only_the_read` and by verify_poolref.rs.

decisions.claim: Only a non-writable allocated section is followed; a GOT entry or a .data pointer is not.
decisions.evidence: The image's copy of a writable slot is the pre-loader value, not what the program reads. The fixture's `reads_slot` loads a `.data` word holding a literal's address and the literal stays unreferenced. This is also why the change is inert on the linked-PIE GOT reads that DIV-102/#328 covers.

decisions.claim: On Cortex-M firmware a handful of the newly-owned rows are short ASCII runs the string scanner extracted from code bytes, colliding with a pool word that holds a Thumb FUNCTION pointer.
decisions.evidence: betaflight has no .rodata (constants live in .text), and three of its 536 newly-owned rows are `' pGpG'`-shaped -- 0x70 0x47 is `bx lr`. The edge itself is true (the pool word does hold that address) and kuna already filed `data` edges to code addresses from materialized constants; what is wrong is calling four code bytes a string. Left alone: narrowing the follow to exclude code targets would drop the function-pointer tables `decompile-all --reachable-from` legitimately uses.

decisions.claim: This closes the direct pool load only. A pool word reached through a register (`add r0,pc; ldr r0,[r0]`) or a GOT-relative ARM PIE load is still unfollowed.
decisions.evidence: The oracle reports 195 u-boot strings and 3 on the witness that a pc-relative pool load reaches and kuna still leaves unowned -- those are in code no descent reached, not shapes the follow declines. No attempt was made to model register-held pool bases; that is picbase's territory and would need the same abstract machine.
